findings.attack: The ledger registers ops-bot (and research-agent) as a service. A prohibition names the same id with the user kind: {type:user,id:ops-bot} forbidding administer ("frozen during the audit"). ops-bot, with a valid root grant, administers realm-config. A variant: research-agent acts for samantha with its read delegation while a prohibition on {user,research-agent} forbids observe. Goal: keep acting through a deny-override because of a kind label, whether that is an admin typo or planted. prohibition_checks matched the holder with Principal.equal (kind + id), so the prohibition applied to nobody.

Ledger principal ids are unique across kinds (a duplicate id is inconsistent_ledger), and the model says honoring an unverified deny is always safe. findings.attack: Decision.t had public fields. Code outside lib/authority takes the Authority.t from a real ALLOW (demo 01: research-agent document:read, grant g-agent-read) and writes `{ deny_03 with verdict = Allow a }`, where deny_03 is the DENY for research-agent admin-surface:administer on realm-config. Codec.decision_to_json then emits a well-formed "decision": "allow" for administer whose authority is a read grant. It can also be written as a record literal from scratch.
findings.initial_result: FAILED (real weakness). Static: `sh test/authority/must_not_compile.sh ocamlc _build-attack-sem/default/lib/authority/.authority.objs/public_cmi _build-attack-sem/default/lib/json/.tjson.objs/byte <snippets>` gave `FAIL allow_in_foreign_decision.ml compiled; it must not` and `FAIL decision_from_scratch.ml compiled; it must not`, exit 1.
findings.fix: The fix is cheap and leaves the wire format unchanged. New lib/authority/decision.mli declares `type t = private {...}`: fields stay readable and matchable, but construction and `{d with ...}` are rejected outside the module. The only constructor is `Decision.make : Mint.seal -> ...`. lib/authority/mint.ml/.mli add an abstract `seal`, and Mint is already a private module, so outside code cannot name Authority__Mint.seal. lib/authority/evaluate.ml builds both decisions through `make Mint.seal`. The verdict type stays public, so the existing must-not-compile expectations are unchanged. After the fix: must_not_compile.sh prints `rejected: Cannot create values of the private type Authority.Decision.t` for both snippets and `Unbound module Authority__Mint` for the seal snippet, and forge.ml no longer compiles against public_cmi. The whole tree still builds and tests (`dune test --force --build-dir _build-attack-sem`, exit 0). Obj.magic remains out of scope.

findings.attack: publisher-bot (or research-agent) holds a document:publish grant with effects [disclose:public] and is prohibited from disclose:public ("automated agents never publish externally"). It publishes q3-report but declares effect disclose:self. A capability has no effect floor, so disclose:self passes the grant bound, the mandate bound and the prohibition, which only covers effects at or above disclose:public. The claim that delegated authority cannot escape a restriction holds only under effect honesty (A1).
findings.initial_result: Pinned test passed: the kernel ALLOWs. `test_adversarial.exe ...` case known_weakness_underdeclared_effect_evades_prohibition gives allow via g-agent-publish. `main.exe scenarios examples/scenarios/adversarial.json --check` gives `ok a43-known_weakness-underdeclared-effect allow`. Declared honestly (disclose:public), the same request is DENY prohibited (a27 and the "downstream-effect: publish declared as disclose:public is prohibited" case).
findings.fix: Not fixed. It is out of reach by construction (threat-model A1, effect honesty). A mitigation such as a per-capability effect floor, or tying an effect to capability or mandate, would change the model and the wire format. Recorded as a known weakness.

findings.attack: research-agent acts for samantha and generates q3-report, declared as produce:organization. research-agent is prohibited from disclose:public. The real consequence of generating is public disclosure (the generator writes to a public location). A request carries exactly one effect, and there is no field for downstream effects: the codec rejects an array of two effects as malformed_request. So the kernel cannot see or refuse the downstream disclosure. Only a separate, honestly declared request (disclose:public) would be denied.
findings.initial_result: Pinned test passed: the kernel ALLOWs via d-agent-generate. `test_adversarial.exe` case known_weakness_downstream_effect_invisible; CLI `ok a42-known_weakness-downstream-effect allow`. The honest declaration gives DENY prohibited. `"effect": [ {...}, {...} ]` gives INDETERMINATE malformed_request (case "downstream-effect: a request cannot declare two effects").
findings.fix: Not fixed. It is out of reach by construction (threat-model: downstream effects, A1). Declaring downstream effects would need a list of effects, or effect composition in the model and wire format.
findings.test: test_adversarial.ml: "known_weakness_downstream_effect_invisible: ...", "downstream-effect: declared honestly, the same step is prohibited", "downstream-effect: a request cannot declare two effects"; adversarial.json: a42-known_weakness-downstream-effect

findings.attack: A purpose-limited grant: research-agent's read grant is usable only under generate-report. A request claiming security-audit (which covers read/observe) is denied with mandate_permitted as the only failed check (a39). But the requester chooses the claim: the same agent asking the same thing and claiming generate-report is ALLOWed. The mandate check therefore binds only an honest client. It is an audit record and an honest-mistake guard, not a control against a dishonest agent.
findings.initial_result: Passed as expected. The model-conforming DENY for the wrong purpose held ("mandate-capability-mismatch: purpose-limited grant claimed under another fitting mandate", deny with only mandate_permitted). findings.attack: Hypothesis S2 reads: "Every DENY names at least one failed check per candidate grant it considered." In a DENY by prohibition, a candidate that would otherwise authorize carries status "authorizes" and zero failed checks. The failed check is in evidence.prohibitions, at request level. An auditor reading the candidate list sees "authorizes" inside a DENY.
findings.initial_result: The strict property fails for prohibition DENYs only. `test_adversarial.exe examples/scenarios/demo.json examples/scenarios/adversarial.json` reports `8 prohibition denies break literal S2` before the fix and `10` after it (the kind-confusion cases became prohibition DENYs). Every such case is a prohibition DENY, which the pinned case asserts. All other DENYs (every candidate refuted with at least one failed check) and all INDETERMINATEs pass the oracle.
findings.fix: Not fixed. Giving each candidate a failed check or a status of its own would change the wire format (new check name or status) and the existing test that every candidate carries exactly 8 checks. The lead can instead read S2 as satisfied by the request-level prohibition check.
findings.test: test_adversarial.ml: "known_weakness_prohibited_deny_has_candidates_without_failed_check: only prohibition denies break literal S2"

findings.attack: A revocation whose `at` (2027-01-01) is after evaluated_at (2026-09-29). Should it already revoke? The model says a revoked grant is invalid and does not mention `at`.
findings.initial_result: Passed as the model is written: DENY, and the leaf is refuted with only `revoked`. `at` is never consulted, only printed (the detail reads "was revoked at 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"). CLI a13 ok.
findings.fix: No change. Ignoring `at` fails closed: an admin typo or wrong timezone in `at` cannot keep a grant alive. Scheduled expiry is expressible with valid_until. A scheduled revocation cannot be expressed as a revocation, and the evidence's "revoked at <future>" wording can puzzle an auditor. The model text should say that `at` is informational.

findings.attack: A property oracle over 131 decisions: 75 built by the attacks plus the 13 demo and 43 adversarial scenarios (56 file requests). It re-derives each answer from the request, not from kernel code. For every ALLOW: all five questions named; the chain starts at a Root whose holder holds the anchor in facts; each link names its parent and its delegator is the parent's holder; each link attenuates (restated independently); every link is within its window and not revoked; the binding assertions; all 8 checks pass; the anchor statement names the root holder. For every decision: the candidate set equals the model's (capability equal, holder is the acting principal or the subject), each candidate has the 8 checks, and its status agrees with its checks. For DENY: prohibited, or no_grant_for_capability, or every candidate refuted with at least one failed check. For insufficient_evidence: no candidate authorizes and one is undetermined. Also, the ablation's reproduction check runs on adversarial.json.
findings.initial_result: Before the fix the only oracle failures were the kind-confusion ALLOWs: `evidence: contradictory-grants: prohibition holder named with the wrong kind ...` and `evidence: adversarial/a31-contra-prohibition-kind-confusion`, both failing on `binding: no prohibition on anyone in the token path covers the effect` (527 tests, 4 failed with both files). `main.exe ablate examples/scenarios/adversarial.json` exited 0: the empty ablation reproduced every verdict from evidence alone.
findings.fix: None beyond prohibition-kind-confusion. After it, all oracle cases pass (527 tests, 0 failed).

notes:
No attack produced a "high" finding: no ALLOW that the model as written forbids. The one fail-open ALLOW, the kind-confused prohibition, is rated medium. It needs a ledger whose prohibition holder has the wrong kind (a trusted admin writes the ledger), and a literal reading of the model says that holder names a different principal. It is fixed.

Fixed within the design:
(1) Prohibition holders now match by id (evaluate.ml).
(2) The principal_kind_mismatch check no longer depends on ledger order (evaluate.ml).
(3) Decision.t is private and its only constructor needs Mint.seal (decision.mli new; decision.ml, mint.ml/.mli, evaluate.ml). The wire format is unchanged, and the verdict type stays public so the existing must-not-compile expectations are untouched. Anyone constructing Decision.t outside lib/authority must now go through Evaluate; nothing in bin/, test/ or the other reviewers' dirs did, and the whole tree builds and tests.

lib/authority excluding the codec grew from 996 to 1070 lines (W6 limit 1500).

Open (pinned as known_weakness_*):
- Under-declared effects escape prohibitions: a capability has no effect floor.
- Downstream effects are invisible: one declared effect per request, and an array of effects is malformed.
- The mandate is a pushed claim.
- Literal S2 fails for prohibition DENYs: the overridden candidates show "authorizes" with no failed check.
- Evidence order follows ledger order. Decisions are permutation-invariant, but 96 of 131 documents change bytes.

Revocation `at`: it is never consulted, so a future-dated revocation revokes now. This fails closed and I kept it; the model should say that `at` is informational.

Doc updates for the lead (not in my paths):
- authority-model.md: prohibitions match their holder by id; Decision.t is private and built only by Evaluate; revocation `at` is informational; clarify how S2 applies to prohibition DENYs.
- threat-model.md and limitations.md refer to docs/adversarial-review.md, which does not exist.

Ablation on adversarial.json (after the fix). 43 scenarios; 40 ablated (3 are well-formedness INDETERMINATE: a24, a35, a36); 29 of those are not allowed.
- who: 15 scenarios, among them a05 (pure deputy), a20 and a21 (reversed or skipped hop), a25, and time or chain cases where the agent's own grant is refuted only by path.
- mandate: 4 scenarios (a02, a04, a39, a40). It is the only flip only in a39 (purpose-limited) and a40 (narrowed mandate).
- effect: 5 scenarios (a27, a28, a29, a31 = prohibitions; a41 = mandate effect bound).
- target: 1 scenario (a07).
- provenance: 15 scenarios (a07-a13, a15, a17, a22, a32-a34, a37, a38).
- a23 (cycle) is flipped only by {who, provenance}.
Realism of mandate as sole decider: a39 is ordinary purpose limitation, but the requester picks the claim, so it only stops honest or mistaken clients. a40 is administrative drift that a ledger lint would catch.

Build isolation: every dune command used --build-dir _build-attack-sem. The Maven run used a scratch copy of keycloak-adapter, so the shared keycloak-adapter/target stayed untouched. During my work test/boundary/dune (the other reviewer) was briefly unbuildable ('Module Test_boundary doesn't exist'), so I built only ./lib ./bin ./test/authority ./examples until the whole tree built again.

adversarial.json was generated by a scratch Python script (not in the repo); the JSON is the source of truth. I ran no git commit, add, stash, checkout or reset, and did not edit docs/hypothesis.md or codec.ml.
